title: Affine pro-etale closed inverse image has an extra left adjoint
statement: Let $i:Z\hookrightarrow X$ be a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion] of affine schemes [def-pc-scheme]. Use the small pro-etale sites and fixed universes of [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], and the inverse image $i^{-1}$ of [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image]. There exists a functor $i^{\mathrm{Sh}}_!:\operatorname{Sh}(Z_{\mathrm{proet}})\to\operatorname{Sh}(X_{\mathrm{proet}})$ with natural bijections $\operatorname{Hom}(i^{\mathrm{Sh}}_!G,F)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(G,i^{-1}F)$ for all sheaves of sets $G$ on $Z_{\mathrm{proet}}$ and $F$ on $X_{\mathrm{proet}}$, with sheaves as in [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology].

proof.text: First handle the quotient immersion q: Spec(A/I) -> Spec(A). Keep sheaves on the full source site X_proet and restrict only the target to Z_app. The restriction res_Z is an equivalence by the existing affine basis and dense-subsite comparison. Put R = q^{-1} followed by res_Z; its right adjoint is res_Z^{-1} followed by q_*, by composition of the ordinary adjunction with the equivalence adjunction.

proof.text: R preserves finite limits. To verify this for the actual constructed q^{-1}, transport the full sites through AsSmall to small categories. The transported base-change functor preserves finite limits. Mathlib lan_preservesFiniteLimits_of_flat and sheafification give left exactness of its sheaf pullback. The transported direct image agrees sectionwise with the original direct image. Uniqueness of left adjoints identifies the transported pullback with the ordinary inverse image. Equivalences and res_Z preserve limits.

proof.text: For weakly contractible V in Z_app, use the sheafified universe-lifted representable of the full-site object v(V). Sheafification adjunction followed by uliftYonedaEquiv gives a natural isomorphism Hom(h_{v(V)}#, F) = F(v(V)). The two clauses of affine_closed_inverseImage_evaluation give the natural comparison between R and sheafified evaluation along v, and bijectivity of the evaluated sheafification unit at V. Hence this unit is an isomorphism of evaluation functors and represents R(-)(V).

proof.text: Let E be the set of weakly contractible objects in Z_app. The stated weakly contractible covering theorem supplies covers by E; their generated sieves cover for the restricted topology by its definition. Apply the existing covering-corepresentable-evaluations criterion. Its SmallCategory interface is handled by ULiftHom: transport the sites, adjunction, finite-limit preservation, covering presieves, and representing sheaves along the explicit equivalences. The canonical precoverage of each transported topology generates that topology; the sites have pullbacks, so all precoverage hypotheses hold. After obtaining a left adjoint of the transported R, cancel the two equivalences to conclude R.IsRightAdjoint. Cancel res_Z to obtain the extra left adjoint of q^{-1}.

source.place: Tag 09BL proof of (3); Tag 0990 affine S_app clause; sites.tex Tag 09YX

proof.text: For an arbitrary affine closed immersion i: Z -> X, compose with X.isoSpec.hom and use Mathlib IsClosedImmersion.Spec_iff to write this composite as e.hom followed by a quotient immersion q. Thus i = e.hom followed by q followed by X.isoSpec.inv. The inverse-image functor of a composite is isomorphic to the composite of inverse images in reverse order: compose the ordinary adjunctions and use the existing direct-image composition isomorphism and left-adjoint uniqueness. For a scheme isomorphism its inverse image is isomorphic to the inverse direct image, by the direct-image equivalence and the same uniqueness. Therefore the two outside inverse images are equivalences, while q^{-1} is a right adjoint by the preceding steps. Their composite, hence i^{-1}, is a right adjoint. Its IsRightAdjoint witness supplies the required functor L and adjunction.
